extracted.intended_audience: Editors and peer reviewers for Sage journals (EMEA) / prospective reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for editors and reviewers on managing peer review, maintaining editorial standards, and using Sage systems and policies when handling manuscript submissions for Sage journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation — select highest quality articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is an effective form of research evaluation to help select the highest quality articles for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review should be used to judge the importance, rigor, and suitability of submissions for the journal's scope; reviewers' assessments inform selection decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity — ensure integrity of the publishing process
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review ensures the integrity of the publishing process and the scholarly record. Reviewers are independent of journal publications and the research being conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should act independently, disclose conflicts of interest, and help protect the reliability of the scholarly record by raising concerns about misconduct or ethical issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality — improve final article through filtering and revision advice
rubrics_metrics.description: The filtering process and revision advice improve the quality of the final research article as well as offering the author new insights into their research methods and the results that they have compiled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should provide constructive, expert feedback to help authors improve methodology, analysis, interpretation and presentation; comments should be actionable and aimed at elevating the paper's quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-anonymized peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-anonymized – the name of the reviewer is hidden from the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that reviewer identities are concealed from authors in this model; tailor comments accordingly and maintain confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-anonymized peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Double-anonymized – names are hidden from both reviewers and the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both parties remain anonymous; reviewers should avoid attempts to identify authors and authors should prepare manuscripts to remove identifying information per journal guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triple-anonymized peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Triple-anonymized – names are hidden from authors, reviewers, and the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extends anonymity to editors as well; follow journal procedures for submission and handling to preserve anonymity across all parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent / open peer review (where offered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage offers a form of open peer review on four journals via our Transparent Peer Review program, whereby the reviews are published alongside the article. The names of the reviewers may also be published, depending on the reviewers’ preference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When participating in transparent peer review, reviewers should be aware their reports may be published and opt in or out per policy; maintain professionalism and clarity in reports intended for public view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication peer review (field-dependent suitability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post publication peer review can offer useful interaction and a discussion forum for the research community. This form of peer review is not usual or appropriate in all fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider disciplinary norms when engaging in or recommending post-publication review; use such forums to continue scholarly dialogue but be mindful of suitability and moderation policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow journal-specific submission and peer review method
rubrics_metrics.description: Please double check the manuscript submission guidelines of the journal you are reviewing in order to ensure that you understand the method of peer review being used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before reviewing, confirm the journal's stated peer review model, formatting and anonymization requirements, and any discipline- or journal-specific review criteria or templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to editorial policies on plagiarism, copyright, ethics and AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage takes issues of copyright infringement, plagiarism or other breaches of best practice in publication very seriously. We seek to protect the rights of our authors and we always investigate claims of plagiarism or misuse of published articles. Equally, we seek to protect the reputation of the journal against malpractice. See Sage's policy on ChatGPT and Generative AI here. Find all of Sage's Editorial Policies here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should flag suspected plagiarism, copyright breaches, or other ethical concerns; be familiar with publisher policies (including AI/GPT usage policies), and report issues to editors rather than attempting to adjudicate them privately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Sage Track for submission and review management
rubrics_metrics.description: Many journals in the Sage portfolio use Sage Track. Sage Track is the Sage-branded ScholarOne online submission and peer review system. Once registered on the journal’s Sage Track website, you will be able to access all invitations and previously reviewed manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register and use Sage Track to receive invitations, submit reports, and access review history. Make use of provided training resources and how‑to videos for effective use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with peer review training and reviewer resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage provides Peer Review Support Resources, a Guide to Becoming a Peer Reviewer, an infographic, and training materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New and experienced reviewers should consult these resources (guides, videos, infographics) to align with expected standards, learn how to write constructive reviews, and understand publisher-specific practices and tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial responsibility for strategic journal development and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: At Sage we work closely with our editors and publishing partners to ensure the strategic editorial development of the journals we publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors are expected to manage the journal, use Editor Gateway/FAQ resources, and make decisions that promote publication of high-quality papers and the journal's strategic goals.
